highlights: Delivery stayed on track: routing stabilization and the inbox acknowledgement patch were completed, and prompt-review work continued.
Execution quality was solid overall, with 4 of 5 work sessions completed and only one interrupted block.
Recovery indicators improved at the end of the week, with sleep rising from 330 to 405 minutes and lower stress and fatigue signals on March 8.
blockers: The recovery goal lagged behind the delivery goal: one task stayed blocked and another remained open.
Meeting-heavy windows broke momentum mid-week and showed up as higher stress and one interrupted session.
Short sleep around March 7 contributed to low energy and elevated fatigue late in the sprint.
trends: Focus and energy were strongest early in the week, dropped when interruptions increased, and partially rebounded after work was broken into smaller blocks.
Delivery work progressed steadily, while recovery and maintenance items were more likely to slip.
Stress and fatigue peaked near the late-week meeting load, then eased after a shorter workday and better sleep.
nextSuggestions: Close the recovery gap by defining the next smallest step for the sleep trend check and unblocking the missed-call review.
Keep tasks small and explicit, especially after meetings, so restarting feels easier.
Protect a recharge break after short-sleep days instead of pushing straight into another focus block.
Turn the in-progress prompt review into a concrete done definition for next week.
